journal.title: Jobs report forecasts, written before looking at Kalshi: P(Sept payrolls > +100K) = 0.38; P(unemployment 4.2% or higher) = 0.33
journal.body:
Written at 4:13 PM ET Thu Oct 1, before reading any prediction-market price. The Sep 30 Kalshi file was not opened. Report: Fri Oct 2, 8:30 AM ET.
Inputs (non-market sources):
- Consensus: payrolls about +90K (Bloomberg survey; BofA 60K; some forecasts 100K); unemployment 4.1%; average hourly earnings +0.3% month on month.
- August: +162K, a five-month high and far above the 31K a month average of the prior 12 months (BLS release, Sep 4). Unemployment 4.1% (unemployed 7.0M). The household survey added 569K jobs and 683K people to the labor force; that jump can reverse.
- September ADP +90K vs 70K expected.
- Initial claims 197K (lowest since July; the 4-week average 200K); continuing claims 1.701M (-11K).
- Challenger layoffs fell in September.
- Analysts flag September education seasonals as a source of volatility.
Payrolls above +100K:
- I center on about +80K. The 12-month trend is weak and August's beat invites payback, partly offset by firm ADP, claims and layoff data.
- First-print surprises have a standard deviation of roughly 75-80K, so P(>100K) is about 0.40. I shade it to 0.38 because of the low 12-month base.
Unemployment 4.2% or higher:
- August's unrounded rate is about 4.10% (7.0M of about 170.7M), so 4.2% needs about +0.05pp.
- The month-to-month change has a standard deviation of about 0.12pp, giving P of about 0.34. Low claims argue against a rise; reversal of the household jump argues for one. 0.33.
Next: run kalshi.py, then record both forecasts with the market mid via forecasts.py add; score after the release.

journal.title: UTHR's own release (7:09 PM ET): it will seek an order pulling Yutrepia's approval; Thursday test unchanged
journal.body:
Source: United Therapeutics release on Business Wire, 7:09 PM ET (stocktitan.net/news/UTHR/united-therapeutics-corporation-prevails-in-patent-litigation-x8g58kv2gmy9.html). It is consistent with the court opinion read for J0024.
New points:
- UTHR says the ruling entitles it to an order under 35 U.S.C. 271(e)(4)(A) directing FDA to withdraw approval of Liquidia's Yutrepia application. It says that could take Yutrepia off the US market entirely, for PAH as well as PH-ILD, until FDA approves a label without PH-ILD. That is broader than the PH-ILD-only recapture in the UTHR dossier.
- UTHR will also seek damages, possibly a royalty on past Yutrepia sales.
- The court gave the parties one week (about Oct 7) to submit an agreed form of final judgment. If they disagree, the court decides the scope.
Caveats:

A multiples-based fair value comes down to two choices. Which earnings: does $12.47 hold without the Q2 tariff refund and after the warrant cost? - Warrants given to a customer are booked as a reduction of revenue as they vest. My rough Black-Scholes value is about $118 per warrant share ($207 price, 7-year life, 50% volatility), about $200M in total, or roughly 2.5% of $8B: a price concession to Amazon on top of the dilution.

journal.title: Evidence check: 241 jumps, noise rule, no $1 floor, breakout triggers withdrawn
journal.body:

Returns are measured against SPY (scripts/jump_study.py, research/movers/study-2026-09-29.json).

- All jumps: median -3.0% over the next 5 sessions and -5.1% over 10. Buying the day after a jump lost to the market in the typical case; the gains sit in a minority of names.
- Noise, the user's volatility idea: stocks with one-year volatility of 120% or more, or 10 or more +/-15% days in the prior year, fell a median 15.7% over 10 sessions, and half lost more than 15%. The rest fell 4.1%. Rule adopted: skip those stocks. A stricter first version (4 or more such days) would have excluded IOVA, VICR and FEIM for no gain.
- Share price: under $1 was no worse than $1-5 (10-session medians -5.6% and -5.1%). The $1 floor was the wrong filter and is gone.
- Market cap: under $100M, median -13.2% over 10 sessions, and 19 of 40 lost more than 15%. Still scanned for visibility, but scored -3.
- Calm stocks of $100M or more with fundamental news (71 jumps): median +0.3% at 5 sessions and -2.4% at 10; 7 of 55 gained more than 15% and 4 lost more than 15%. On average the market priced the news on day one.
- Entry timing, calm stocks of $100M or more: buying at the first new post-jump closing high did worse than buying at the jump-day close (5-session median -2.2% vs -1.1%, up in 21 of 61 vs 52 of 117).

Decision: the breakout triggers in J0013/J0004 (GNRC above $213, VICR above $292, SEI above $71, FEIM above $89) are withdrawn. These names stay on watch without a buy rule. The scan feeds research, not this week's entries. Scheduled catalysts (Micron, Nike, the jobs report) and the positions we hold stay the plan.

By cause of the jump:

So jumps on real news usually hold (51 of 76 held or extended), but the typical name does not keep drifting within a few weeks; the gains come from the roughly one in five that extend. journal.title: Big-mover catalyst scan: method and Sep 29 verdicts
journal.body:
New daily screen (scripts/movers.py): every US stock up 10-15%+ on the day with real volume. For each one it pulls the headlines and filings, market cap, revenue, growth, EV/sales, relative volume, short interest and analyst targets, then tags the likely cause. The rule it tests: big moves on material news (a raised guide, an order that is large relative to the company, a refinancing that removes default risk, an approval) tend to keep drifting. Moves on no news, cash takeovers (capped at the deal price), de-SPACs and financings (new shares sold into the spike) do not. Scans are saved to research/movers/ and followed up (--follow-up) so the idea is measured on our own data.

Sep 29 scan: 44 stocks up 10%+, 23 above $100M market cap. Verdicts:
- IOVA +31.5% (held in the H-1B book): raised its 2026 revenue guide to $410-420M (about +60%), and UBS and HC Wainwright raised targets. A real re-rating. The risk is valuation: EV/sales is about 19x trailing and the stock sits above the old average target ($12.40), so further gains need estimates to keep rising. Hold with the $12.35 stop.
- JELD +12.4% ($1.99, $173M market cap on $3.15B revenue): 2027 notes and 2028 term loans extended to 2031 plus $135M of new first-lien money; 94.5% of noteholders and 72.2% of term lenders committed; no equity in the release. This is the "long-standing problem solved" case. Against it: the new debt ranks ahead of today's creditors and likely costs more, housing demand is weak with yields at multi-year highs, the exchange offers haven't launched, and the average analyst target is $1.93. Re-ratings like this take weeks. Watchlist; the trigger is exchange-offer terms with no equity dilution and the stock holding above $1.90.
- CCL +13.4%: record Q3 revenue, record $7.6B of deposits, raised guidance. A classic post-earnings drift candidate, but a $34B company won't double. Watch for trend days.
- ITG +15.5%: a rebound after a -32% day caused by a large holder exiting after the July IPO. Organic growth is weak and Comcast and Charter are 53% of revenue. Pass.
- WW +13.8%: a Google Fitbit employer-program tie-up for a post-bankruptcy company with a $171M market cap. Small news. Pass for now.
- PWP +11.8%: deal-activity and insider-buying chatter, no hard catalyst. Pass.
- SDEV +108%: no news (the company said so) and -21% after hours. The no-news reversal case in action.
- SANG +37%: cash takeover by BRC, capped. Pass. NAUT +23%: an analyst initiation only. ONEN +22%: de-SPAC on the nuclear theme. BGIN, EGG, SVRN: thin, no fundamental news. All pass.

Use in this challenge: the drift plays out over weeks and we have four sessions, so the scan supplies candidates and a day-two entry needs confirmation: holding above the prior close through the first 30-60 minutes, relative volume above 2 and no offering filed.

journal.title: Rule change: extended hours and news trading
journal.body:
Per the owner's instruction, the only limits now are legal ones for an H-1B holder.

- Dropped my self-imposed caps: 6 orders a day, 30 in total, 3 day trades per 5 days, and 60% per position. A 25-orders-a-day fuse stays, only to stop a runaway loop.
- Trading hours are now 4:00 AM to 8:00 PM ET: pre-market, regular and after-hours. Extended-hours fills use the latest extended-hours print plus wider slippage (25/50/100 bps by price). The 8 PM to 4 AM overnight session isn't simulated because there's no reliable price feed for it.
- The H-1B line: frequently trading your own account is still investing. Unauthorized self-employment would mean trading for others, being paid for it, or running it as a business (for example electing trader tax status). None of that applies here.
- Still binding, because that's how a $1,000 cash account works: no margin or shorting, and T+1 settlement (shares bought with unsettled sale proceeds can't be sold until those proceeds settle).

News trading setup:
- The data job scans trending tickers, top gainers and most-active stocks every 15 minutes from 6 AM to 8 PM ET, and flags movers of 6% or more (4% or more in extended hours) plus any new headlines.
- Checks run every 15 minutes during the session and every 30 minutes in extended hours. Event checks are scheduled for Micron's report (Wed 4:07 PM), Nike's (Thu 4:18 PM) and the jobs report (Fri 8:33 AM).
- Rules for news trades: act on fresh, material news with confirmed volume; don't chase a spike that is already fading; same stop discipline as every other position.

Pre-market Tuesday: NVTS (US Army silicon-carbide program, +12% after hours) and SMMT (+18% after hours, news to confirm) are candidates if they hold their gains on volume.

Exit rules, checked at every hourly review:
- Stops: -15% on 2x ETFs and -12% on single stocks, measured from entry.
- At +25% on a position, sell a third and move the stop on the rest to breakeven.
- Losers are never averaged down. Winners get added to, from cash.

If Iran escalates overnight and the market gaps down more than 1.5%, entries shrink by half and wait for the first hour's low.

- AMD / AMDL (2x): 1% off its record, 20-day +32%; bought World Labs for $8.2B. OpenAI is a major customer, which is a risk after the pause.
- MSTR / MSTU (2x): 60-day +70% / +131%; tracks bitcoin into seasonally strong October.
- Watching, not buying: VG (80% of float short but trending down), tankers and UCO (escalation hedge), NKE (earnings Thu at a 12-year low), TSLA and TSLL (deliveries Fri).

journal.title: Week ahead: macro backdrop and calendar
journal.body:
Stocks fell Monday: S&P 500 -0.77% to 7,683.69, Nasdaq -0.92%. Three reasons: Trump rejected Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the 10-year yield hit 5.24% (highest since 2007), and OpenAI paused training of its top models, which knocked memory and chip stocks (MU -2.6%, INTC -5.7%, SOXL -6%). NVDA gained 1.7% on a $150B buyback add.

- Fed hiked 25 bp on Sep 16 to 3.75-4.00%; futures price roughly 2-in-3 odds of another hike Oct 28. August CPI 3.4% y/y.
- Brent near $105 with Hormuz largely closed. Talks may resume this week (CBS) but the WSJ reports Trump privately expects renewed bombing. This is the week's biggest two-way risk.
- No shutdown risk: government funded through Dec 11.
- Calendar: Tue JOLTS and consumer confidence; Wed ADP, August PCE, quarter-end, Micron earnings after the close; Thu ISM manufacturing, Nike after the close; Fri September payrolls (consensus +90k) and Tesla Q3 deliveries (consensus ~454k); Mon ISM services.
- Bitcoin about $83K. Strategy (MSTR) bought another $143M of BTC on Monday.
